knowledge_point.title: Using the Pythagorean Theorem on the Unit Circle

question.:question/problem: The point $A$ is located in the first quadrant and lies on the unit circle. The $y$-coordinate of $A$ is $\frac{\sqrt{43}}{7}.$ What is the $x$-coordinate of $A?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Since the point $A$ lies on the unit circle, it must satisfy the Pythagorean theorem: 

$$
{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=1
$$

Substituting $y=\frac{\sqrt{43}}{7}$ into the above and solving for $x$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2} & =1 \\ {x}^{2}+{(\frac{\sqrt{43}}{7})}^{2} & =1 \\ {x}^{2}+(\frac{43}{49}) & =1 \\ {x}^{2} & =1-\frac{43}{49} \\ {x}^{2} & =\frac{6}{49} \\ x & =\sqrt{\frac{6}{49}} \\ x & =\pm \frac{\sqrt{6}}{7}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $A$ lies in the first quadrant, $x$ must be positive, so we select the positive answer. Therefore, our final answer is $x=\frac{\sqrt{6}}{7}.$
